qualification: Pre-fix parse_track skipped sample_index(&stbl, ...) whenever fragmented was true, dropping any initial samples in moov/stbl and ignoring corrupt stbl tables, while index_fragments only updated track.duration when track.duration == 0. Pre-fix baseline reproduced all three defects and all 4 forced acceptance tests failed.

Validating and indexing moov/stbl in fragmented tracks (using expanded_index so moof/traf samples append directly to the initial sample table) and extending track.duration = track.duration.max(stated.unwrap_or(0)) preserves all initial + fragment samples, implicit tfdt continuation from stbl, and refuses corrupt init stbl tables as Error::Invalid before native decoder admission.

All 4 healthy controls (regular MP4, empty-init 3-fragment fMP4, 1-in-stbl + 2-explicit-tfdt-fragments, and 2-in-stbl + 1-implicit-tfdt-fragment) retain exact coded packets, sync flags, 50 Hz clocks, sample/packet budgets, analytic 16x16 VP9 planes/RGB (128/130), 32 total public clamped seek targets, rewind, and repeated EOF.
4 focused tests, 78 related MP4/HLS/VP9 integration tests, 17 MP4 unit tests, 37 minimal-configuration (--no-default-features) tests, offline fixture generator unittest, and full player build pass.

ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015, 8.8.4 and 8.8.8 specify that movie fragments extend tracks defined in moov after any initial samples in moov/stbl. All fixtures are pure synthetic offline VP9/fMP4 files requiring neither FFmpeg nor network access.
counting: One fragmented MP4 hybrid moov/stbl + moof/traf indexing and validation fix (FVID-0184). No extra IDs for individual hybrid/corrupt variants, controls, or fixture generator.
